# Answer key: polyglot services (C#, Go, Rust, Java)

Area root: `services/`. Paths below are relative to `sample-app/`.

Files:
- `services/labels/LabelService.cs`, `services/labels/Labels.csproj` (C#, net8.0, Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 5.2.2, Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions 8.0.2)
- `services/inventory/inventory.go`, `services/inventory/go.mod` (Go, `package main`, stdlib only)
- `services/checksum/src/lib.rs`, `services/checksum/Cargo.toml` (Rust library crate, no dependencies)
- `services/erp-sync/src/main/java/com/batchtrack/ErpSync.java` (Java 17+, JDK only; a JDBC driver such as sqlite-jdbc is supplied at runtime)

What was checked when the fixture was built (in scratch copies, so no build output sits in the fixture):
- C#: `dotnet build` (SDK 8.0.425) succeeds. The default analyzers raise only CA2200, which is PG-06. With `AnalysisLevel=latest-recommended` they also raise CA1848 (use LoggerMessage) and CA1305 on `RenderZpl`. Neither of those is seeded; see FP-PG-04.
- Go: `go vet` is clean and `go build` succeeds. A probe test run with `-race` reported `WARNING: DATA RACE` in `Reconcile` (PG-10). In a separate probe, 10 timed-out `onHandWithin` calls left 10 extra goroutines alive (PG-07).
- Rust: `cargo test` passes the 3 existing unit tests, and `cargo clippy --all-targets` shows no warnings. In debug, `fletcher16(b"abcde")` panics with "attempt to add with overflow". In release it returns 0xC3EF where 0xC8F0 is correct (PG-15). `verify_label("PX-2026-0101/X")` panics in `unwrap` (PG-12), and `verify_label("PX20260101/9")` panics with "malformed batch number" (PG-14).
- Java: `javac -Xlint:all` compiles with exactly one warning, `[overrides] ... overrides equals, but neither it nor any superclass overrides hashCode` (PG-17). A probe confirmed that `Stream.of(b1, b2).distinct().count()` is 2 for two equal batches. Calling `toJson` from 8 threads produced tens of thousands of wrong posting dates in 160,000 calls (21,478 and 46,305 in two runs; the count varies) (PG-18).

## Seeded defects

| ID | File | Location | Category | Description | Correct fix |
|----|------|----------|----------|-------------|-------------|
| PG-01 | services/labels/LabelService.cs | `Reprint` (l.146) `public async void Reprint(...)` | C# async / error handling | A public, non-event-handler method is `async void`. Callers cannot await it or observe completion, and an exception from `FindLotLabelAsync` (SqlException) or `SendToPrinterAsync` (HttpRequestException) goes to the thread pool or SynchronizationContext unobserved, which crashes the process. | Make it `public async Task ReprintAsync(...)` and have callers await it. |
| PG-02 | services/labels/LabelService.cs | `Preview` (l.142) `FindLotLabelAsync(batchNo, lotNo).Result` | C# async / sync-over-async | The method blocks on an async method with `.Result`. `FindLotLabelAsync` awaits without `ConfigureAwait(false)`, so a caller on a UI or legacy ASP.NET SynchronizationContext (such as the label station UI) deadlocks. Elsewhere it ties up a thread-pool thread, and failures arrive wrapped in `AggregateException`. | Make it `public async Task<string> PreviewAsync(...)` with `var label = await FindLotLabelAsync(...)`, making callers async all the way up. `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` is not a fix. |
| PG-03 | services/labels/LabelService.cs | `SendToPrinterAsync` (l.115) `using (var client = new HttpClient { ... })` | C# resource management / HttpClient misuse | A new `HttpClient` is created and disposed on every print job. Each one opens its own connection, which is left in TIME_WAIT, so batch printing and held-label release can exhaust sockets, and no connection pooling or DNS refresh happens. | Inject one long-lived `HttpClient` (typed client via `IHttpClientFactory`, or a single static or instance client with `BaseAddress`/`Timeout` set once) and reuse it. |
| PG-04 | services/labels/LabelService.cs | `FindLotLabelAsync` (l.71-72) | Security / SQL injection (CWE-89) | `batchNo` and `lotNo`, which are operator or scanner input, are concatenated into the SQL text, e.g. `lotNo = "x' OR '1'='1"`. `GetBatchLabelsAsync` in the same class uses a parameter correctly. | Use parameters: `"... WHERE b.batch_no = @batchNo AND m.lot_no = @lotNo"`, with `cmd.Parameters.Add("@batchNo", SqlDbType.NVarChar, 64).Value = batchNo;` and the same for `@lotNo`. |
| PG-05 | services/labels/LabelService.cs | `WriteToSpool` (l.107-109) `var writer = new StreamWriter(...)` | C# resource management / IDisposable | The `StreamWriter` and its `FileStream` are never disposed. The OS file handle stays open until a GC finalizer runs. On Windows the spool file stays locked (the spooler agent cannot pick it up or delete it), and printing the same batch again throws an IOException ("file is being used by another process"). On Linux the second open succeeds, but handles still pile up until the finalizer runs. | `using var writer = new StreamWriter(path, false, Utf8);` or simply `File.WriteAllText(path, RenderZpl(label), Utf8);`. |
| PG-06 | services/labels/LabelService.cs | `PrintBatchAsync` catch block (l.133-137) `throw ex;` | C# exception handling | `throw ex;` resets the stack trace to this frame, so the original failure site in SqlClient, HttpClient or the file IO is lost. CA2200 flags it. | Use `throw;`. Alternatively, wrap it: `throw new LabelPrintException(..., ex)`. |
| PG-07 | services/inventory/inventory.go | `onHandWithin` (l.85-97) `ch := make(chan result)` | Go concurrency / goroutine leak | The channel is unbuffered. When the timeout fires first, `select` returns via `ctx.Done()` and nobody ever receives from `ch`, so the worker goroutine blocks forever on `ch <- result{...}`. That leaks one goroutine per timed-out lot per run. | Use a buffer of 1, `ch := make(chan result, 1)`. Or drop the goroutine and call `c.OnHand(ctx, lotNo)` directly, since it already honors `ctx`. |
| PG-08 | services/inventory/inventory.go | `WriteReport` (l.165-167) `_ = enc.Encode(found)`, `_ = f.Close()`, `return nil` | Go error handling (ignored errors) | Encode and Close errors (disk full, NFS write-back on close) are thrown away and the function returns nil. A truncated or empty `discrepancies.json` is reported as success ("checked N lots"). | `if err := enc.Encode(found); err != nil { f.Close(); return err }` then `return f.Close()`, or use `errors.Join`. |
| PG-09 | services/inventory/inventory.go | `LoadLots` (l.150) `qty, _ := strconv.ParseFloat(rec[2], 64)` | Go error handling (ignored errors) / data integrity | A malformed quantity (`"1,234"`, `""`, `"12.5kg"`) is silently read as 0. The lot is then reported as a false discrepancy, or a genuine quantity is lost. | `qty, err := strconv.ParseFloat(rec[2], 64); if err != nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: lot %s: bad qty %q: %w", path, rec[0], rec[2], err) }` |
| PG-10 | services/inventory/inventory.go | `Reconcile` (l.118) `found[lot.LotNo] = Discrepancy{...}` | Go concurrency / data race | Up to 8 goroutines write to the shared `found` map with no synchronization. `-race` reports a DATA RACE, and at runtime it can abort with `fatal error: concurrent map writes`. | Guard the write with a `sync.Mutex` (`mu.Lock(); found[...] = ...; mu.Unlock()`). Or send results over a channel and write the map from a single goroutine. |
| PG-11 | services/inventory/inventory.go | `LoadLots` (l.135) `defer f.Close()` inside `for _, path := range paths` | Go resource management | A defer inside a loop runs only when `LoadLots` returns, so every export file stays open until all of them are read. With many exports this hits the fd limit ("too many open files"). | Move the per-file work into a helper such as `func loadFile(path string) ([]Lot, error)` that has `defer f.Close()`, or close explicitly at the end of each iteration. |
| PG-12 | services/checksum/src/lib.rs | `verify_label` (l.74) `let found: u8 = digit.parse().unwrap();` | Rust error handling / panic on untrusted input | The check digit comes from a scanned label, and `.unwrap()` panics on any misread (`"PX-2026-0101/X"`, a trailing `/`, `"/999"`), even though the function returns `Result`. | `let found: u8 = digit.parse().map_err(\|_\| ChecksumError::Malformed(scanned.to_string()))?;` |
| PG-13 | services/checksum/src/lib.rs | `sign_export` (l.118) `let rec = line.clone();` | Rust performance / needless allocation | The loop deep-clones every `RecordLine` (three `String`s) for each line of an export only to call `canonical(&self)`, which borrows. That is pointless allocation in the hot loop. | `let body = line.canonical();` with no clone. |
| PG-14 | services/checksum/src/lib.rs | `parse_batch_no` (l.42-43) `panic!("malformed batch number: {s}")` | Rust error handling / panic in Result-returning fn | A wrong number of `-`-separated parts is an expected input error, and the function already returns `Result` with `ChecksumError::Malformed` for its other failures, but here it panics. `verify_label("PX20260101/9")` panics. | `return Err(ChecksumError::Malformed(s.to_string()));` |
| PG-15 | services/checksum/src/lib.rs | `fletcher16` (l.85-89) `let mut sum1: u8`, `sum1 = (sum1 + b) % 255` | Rust arithmetic overflow / incorrect checksum | The Fletcher-16 accumulators are `u8`, so `sum1 + b` and `sum2 + sum1` overflow whenever the running sum passes 255. In debug builds that panics ("attempt to add with overflow") on practically every real record line. In release it wraps mod 256 before `% 255`, producing non-standard checksums: `b"abcde"` gives 0xC3EF instead of 0xC8F0, so the ERP rejects the lines. | Use wider accumulators: `let mut sum1: u16 = 0; let mut sum2: u16 = 0; ... sum1 = (sum1 + b as u16) % 255; sum2 = (sum2 + sum1) % 255; (sum2 << 8) \| sum1`. Changing to `wrapping_add` is NOT a correct fix, because it still computes mod 256. Test vectors: "abcde" = 0xC8F0, "abcdef" = 0x2057, "abcdefgh" = 0x0627. |
| PG-16 | services/erp-sync/src/main/java/com/batchtrack/ErpSync.java | `loadPending` (l.75-91) | Java resource leak (JDBC) | The `Connection` and `PreparedStatement` are never closed. Only the `ResultSet` is, and only on the happy path. Every 5-minute cycle leaks a connection and statement, holding SQLite file handles and locks, or exhausting a server connection pool. | `try (Connection conn = ...; PreparedStatement ps = conn.prepareStatement(...)) { ps.setString(...); try (ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery()) { ... } }` |
| PG-17 | services/erp-sync/src/main/java/com/batchtrack/ErpSync.java | `ReleasedBatch.equals` (l.64-70), no `hashCode`; relied on by `.distinct()` in `syncAll` (l.97) | Java equals/hashCode contract | `equals` is overridden without `hashCode`. The query JOINs `signatures`, so a batch with more than one `approved` signature comes back as several rows. `.distinct()` (hash-based) is meant to collapse them, but with identity hash codes it keeps them all, so the batch is posted twice and the ERP books a duplicate goods receipt. | Add `@Override public int hashCode() { return Objects.hash(id, batchNo); }`. Optionally also replace the JOIN with `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM signatures s WHERE s.batch_id = b.id AND s.meaning = 'approved')`. A Java `record` is also fine. |
| PG-18 | services/erp-sync/src/main/java/com/batchtrack/ErpSync.java | `ERP_DATE` (l.34), used in `toJson` (l.181) from pool threads via `postSite` | Java thread safety | A `static final SimpleDateFormat` is shared by the 4 pool threads that build per-site payloads concurrently. `SimpleDateFormat` is not thread-safe, which gives corrupted or wrong `postingDate` values and occasional exceptions. | Use `DateTimeFormatter.ISO_OFFSET_DATE_TIME`, which is immutable and thread-safe, with `OffsetDateTime`/`Instant` in place of `Date`. Otherwise a `ThreadLocal<SimpleDateFormat>` or a new instance per call. |
| PG-19 | services/erp-sync/src/main/java/com/batchtrack/ErpSync.java | `postSite` (l.109-114) `payload += ...` in a loop | Java performance | Building the payload with `String +=` inside the loop is O(n^2) copying. On first sync, a site with thousands of released batches builds a multi-MB payload this way. | `StringBuilder`, or `batches.stream().map(ErpSync::toJson).collect(Collectors.joining(",", "[", "]"))`. |
| PG-20 | services/erp-sync/src/main/java/com/batchtrack/ErpSync.java | `postWithRetry` catch (l.147-148) and `pause` (l.159-160) | Java concurrency / swallowed InterruptedException | `InterruptedException` is only logged. The interrupt flag is not restored and the retry loop carries on, so `close()` (`shutdownNow()`) and main-thread interruption cannot stop in-flight retries: up to 5 attempts with backoff continue after shutdown was requested. | Restore the interrupt flag and stop: `catch (InterruptedException e) { Thread.currentThread().interrupt(); return false; }`. Let `pause` propagate the exception or re-interrupt, and have the caller check `Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted()`. |

## Deliberately correct code (false-positive traps)

| ID | File | Location | Why it is correct |
|----|------|----------|-------------------|
| FP-PG-01 | services/labels/LabelService.cs | `OnPrinterStatusChanged` (l.160) `private async void` | This is an event handler subscribed to `IPrinterMonitor.StatusChanged` in the constructor. `async void` is the required and accepted form for event handlers, and every await sits inside a try/catch, so nothing escapes. It should not be reported as PG-01. |
| FP-PG-02 | services/labels/LabelService.cs | `OnPrinterStatusChanged` catch (l.175) `catch (Exception ex)` | A broad catch is correct at the top of an async void event handler. It logs and re-queues the job and does not rethrow. |
| FP-PG-03 | services/labels/LabelService.cs | `GetBatchLabelsAsync` (l.62-63) | The query is parameterized (`@batchId`, `SqlDbType.Int`). The shared `LabelQuery` constant holds no user input. |
| FP-PG-04 | services/labels/LabelService.cs | `RenderZpl` (l.89-100) | The quantity is formatted with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`, and the interpolated `AppendLine`s only insert strings, so the CA1305 analyzer warning is noise. `Field()` strips the ZPL control characters `^` and `~`, and `Utf8` is BOM-less on purpose. |
| FP-PG-05 | services/inventory/inventory.go | `OnHand` (l.63) `defer resp.Body.Close()` | The defer is scoped to the function, one per request, not inside a loop. The status is checked before decoding and the path segment is escaped with `url.PathEscape`. |
| FP-PG-06 | services/inventory/inventory.go | `Reconcile` (l.101-125) `errs` / `sem` / `return found, <-errs` | `errs` is buffered to `len(lots)`, so sends never block. `sem` bounds concurrency to 8. After `close(errs)`, `<-errs` yields the first error, or nil when there was none. `wg.Add(1)` comes before `go`. |
| FP-PG-07 | services/checksum/src/lib.rs | `lrc` (l.95-96) `wrapping_add` / `wrapping_neg` | The LRC is defined modulo 256, so wrapping arithmetic is exactly right here. `lrc(&[]) == 0` and `lrc(&[1, 2]) == 0xFD` are tested. It contrasts with PG-15. |
| FP-PG-08 | services/checksum/src/lib.rs | `verify_line` (l.127-138); `check_digit` (l.56) `unwrap_or(0)` | `verify_line` maps parse errors into `ChecksumError::Malformed` correctly. In `check_digit`, `to_digit` runs on characters of a `format!`ted integer, so it cannot fail. The `.unwrap()`s at l.146 and l.152 are inside `#[cfg(test)]`. |
| FP-PG-09 | services/erp-sync/src/main/java/com/batchtrack/ErpSync.java | `recordAudit` (l.164-174) | This path uses try-with-resources correctly with a parameterized INSERT. It contrasts with PG-16. |
| FP-PG-10 | services/erp-sync/src/main/java/com/batchtrack/ErpSync.java | `close()` (l.203-214) | `InterruptedException` is handled correctly: `shutdownNow()` plus `Thread.currentThread().interrupt()`. It contrasts with PG-20. |
| FP-PG-11 | services/erp-sync/src/main/java/com/batchtrack/ErpSync.java | `quote` (l.184-201); `toJson` (l.176-182) | `quote` is correct JSON string escaping with a `StringBuilder`, so the hand-built JSON is not an injection issue. `toJson` concatenates a fixed number of strings with no loop, which the compiler optimizes, so it is not a PG-19 instance. |

## Not seeded (acceptable extra observations; neither required nor penalized)
- C#: CA1848 (LoggerMessage delegates) is a performance and style nit. The missing `CancellationToken` parameters on the async methods are also a nit.
- Go: `Reconcile` returns partial results alongside the first error by design, and `run` logs and continues.
- C#: `ReadLabelsAsync` calls `GetString`/`GetDouble` without null checks, but `batches.product` and `materials.qty` are nullable in the schema, so a row with a NULL there throws `SqlNullValueException`.
- Java: if `recordAudit` fails after a successful post, the next cycle posts that batch again (this is logged). `syncAll` lets `SQLException` end the main loop. `batches.site` is nullable, and `Collectors.groupingBy(b -> b.site)` throws `NullPointerException` ("element cannot be mapped to a null key") for a batch with no site. A JDBC driver dependency or build file for erp-sync is not included.
- Rust: `sign_export` allocates one `String` per line via `format!`, which is expected.
